title: Wire Drawing Bench
pages: Craft the controller from two grindstones, a solar tempered plate from the Solar Smelter, two chains, a Wire Draw Die in the centre, two sealed steel plates and an Assay Bead from the Assay Cupel Hearth. Place any anvil (chipped and damaged ones work) directly beneath it a grindstone directly against its east and west sides, a grindstone two blocks out to the north and to the south (leaving the north and south faces open), and one iron-bar guard directly above every grindstone; grindstones may face any way. The raised guards keep hands clear of the rotating capstans. It is a tier-5 device: its Rhenium Filament replaces the rhenium ingots in the Enamel Kiln recipe, and the kiln's Heliograph Plate is needed for the Heliostat Etcher.

The Wire Draw Die is the bench's working head: real drawing dies pull wire through a hard, polished hole, so it is a cemented carbide nib shrink-fit into a steel casing. Mix four tungsten grit, one cobalt grit (the binder) and any coal or charcoal (the carbon) into 2 Carbide Powder Blend. The Copper Hot Press sinters 2 blend into a Cemented Carbide Nib (240 ticks, 16 FE/t; hoppers can feed it). Surround the nib with four Tempered Steel from the Quench Vat in a plus shape to make the die. A bare anvil, nib or steel cannot stand in for it.

Hold a metal batch in your main hand and right-click the formed controller. Each pull loads the listed ingot count into the bench's stock buffer and adds the listed hunger exhaustion to you at once; the capstans then draw it over 40 ticks and an empty-hand click collects the product. While a batch is still loaded the bench refuses another pull without taking items or hunger. Exhaustion ranges from 0.8 for a chain to 4.0 for a chainmail chestplate. Drawing is hard work: with a food level below 7 (when you can no longer sprint) the bench refuses and asks you to eat. Inputs are item tags (forge:ingots/<metal>), so any mod's matching ingot works. A missing guard, grindstone or anvil stops the bench without using anything.

It runs 24 datapack wire drawing recipes, each with a different stock. Two tagged copper ingots give two Drawn Copper Tubes for the Silvering Bath circulation loop. The die represents the drawing of an already pierced tube shell; piercing and wall-thickness control are abstracted. One Tool Steel Stock (ground from tool steel) is drawn and wound over the bench mandrel into 4 Coil Springs for the Spectral Loom treadles. One tagged iron ingot gives a Drawn Iron Rod, which the Induction Coiler anneals into the Soft-Iron Plunger of a Solenoid. One rhenium ingot gives a Rhenium Filament. One kiln-fired Nichrome Billet gives 2 Nichrome Resistance Wire for the Phase Annealer heating element. Three nickel give 8 iron bars; zinc 2 chains; lead a lead (leash); platinum a lightning rod; two silver a clock; four cobalt a compass; two tungsten a heavy and two aluminum a light weighted pressure plate. Six molybdenum, antimony or manganese give 6 powered, detector or activator rails. Chainmail, otherwise uncraftable, is drawn from eight titanium (chestplate), seven chromium (leggings), five osmium (helmet) or four tantalum (boots). Ruthenium gives 2 tripwire hooks, three rhodium a crossbow, two germanium a fishing rod and one tin a lantern.

Automation: face a hopper or pipe into the open north side (or the top) and pull finished wire from the open south side; sneak-right-click an empty hand on a face to cycle input, output or disabled (the south face starts as input, so switch it to output once). A formed bench draws one buffered batch every 40 ticks with the capstans doing the work, so automated pulls cost nobody hunger; stored stock and product survive reload and drop if the bench is broken, and a missing grindstone, guard or anvil pauses the buffer. An empty-hand click collects the product. Hand pulls load the same buffer and timer. When two recipes match, the lowest recipe id wins. Creative players draw without exhaustion. JEI's Wire Drawing category lists ingot counts, tags, outputs and exhaustion per pull, with the bench as catalyst.
